newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Troops from Togo, Chad, Morocco due in Zaire-aide.
newsitem.headline: Troops from Togo, Chad, Morocco due in Zaire-aide.

text.p: Zaire has chartered planes to bring in troops from African allies Morocco, Togo and Chad to help its army in a spreading rebel war, a senior Zaire defence ministry official said on Monday.
"Togo, Morocco and Chad are all prepared to send troops along with materials. Egypt has offered materials mostly to equip the infantry," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
"The planes for this operation have already been chartered," the official said. He could not give a definite date for the arrival of the foreign troops.
Tutsi-led rebels battling the Zaire army since October have extended their campaign and territory they hold from the borders of Rwanda and Uganda to Zaire's mineral-rich Shaba Province.
A defence official said earlier the army was battling to hold on to the lake-side town of Kalemie. Rebel and military sources said the interior port town had already fallen.

Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of fighting along with ethnic Tutsis who launched an armed rebellion after local authorities threatened to expel them to their ancestral homeland in Rwanda. Rebel leaders now say their objective is to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko who has ruled Zaire since 1965.
Mobutu, who has been convalescing in France from cancer surgery, arrived in Morocco for a three-day visit and talks with long-time ally King Hassan expected to centre on the fighting.

Moroccan troops helped put down a 1977 secessionist uprising in Shaba after Zairean forces were overwhelmed. They also relieved French and Belgian paratroops backing Zairean authorities in the mining town of Kolwezi the following year.
The defence official said Zaire had started a nationwide recruitment campaign for the army to train up 13 rapid intervention commando brigades of 2,000 men each.

Siganalling the widening international scope of the conflict in the heart of Africa, the official added that China and Israel would help train the commandos at bases in the Zaire provinces of Shaba, Upper Zaire and Equateur.
